if the second largest eigenvalue of the pseudo-random r-regular graph satisfies λ = o(n−1/2r3/2), then a random subgraph H of G with edge density at least 1−o(r2/2) has a Hamilton cycle, and if λ = o(r−1/2(n−1/4)−1/2(logn−1/4)), then H has a Hamilton cycle for almost all order of the edges of H.
the threshold for the Hamiltonicity of the random subgraph of G is at least (r5/2/(log n)3/2) and that it is o(1) for any fixed r.

if the eigenvalues of G satisfy the condition λ = o(r2/n), then the threshold for the Hamilton cycle in a subgraph of G is at least n/2, and if the eigenvalues satisfy the condition λ=o(r5/2/n3/2), then the threshold is at most n/2.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following problem: Given an r- regular graph G on nvertices with a Hamilton cycle and an edge ordering of G. At which point in the process of inserting edges of the graph G one by one according the given order the first random subgraph of G with a Hamilton cycle is obtained?
the following problem: Given an r- regular graph G on nvertices with a Hamilton cycle. Order its edges randomly and add them one by one, according to the chosen ordering, to the empty graph.
the following questions: Given a pseudo-random graph, how many random edges should we insert to guarantee the appearance of a random Hamilton cycle?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the threshold for the Hamiltonicity in a random sub graph of an arbitrary r-regular graph is at least r5/2/( n3/2(log n)3/2), which is the best known bound for the Hamiltonicity threshold for arbitrary graphs.
the appearance of a random Hamilton cycle in G is equivalent to the appearance of a spanning tree with all vertices of degree two or more in the random subgraph H.

for almost all order of the edges of a pseudo-random r-regular graph with a Hamilton cycle the random subgraph H* of G, obtained at the very moment, when the degrees of all vertices in H* become at least two has a Hamilton cycle, if r=Ω(n1/2(log n)1/2) and the eigenvalue of G with the largest absolute value is bounded by λ=o(r3/(n(logn)3)).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we prove the existence of a Hamilton cycle at the very moment of the appearance of the giant component in a random subgraphs of a regular pseudo-random graph.
if the eigenvalues of a graph G are sufficiently small and if G is pseudo-random then a random subgraph H of G has a Hamilton cycle if the number of edges of H satisfies |E(H)| ≥ 1.5r2n(logn)3.
we prove that the threshold for the Hamilton cycle in a subgraph of a graph with a large second eigenvalue is of the same order as the threshold for the existence of a Hamilton cycle.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the eigenvalues of a pseudo-random r-regular graph are not the only factor determining the appearance of Hamilton cycles in random subgraph of G. We show that for a pseudo-random graph, the eigenvalue with the second largest modulus is the most influential factor, but it is not the only one.
the threshold for the existence of Hamilton cycles in random subgraph of pseudo-random graphs can be much smaller than the threshold for Hamilton cycles in the Erdös-Rényi random graphs G(n,p).
the value of the second eigenvalue of the graph is the main factor determining the threshold for the Hamiltonicity of a random subgraph.
